text: When a GateMate transposed FIR is timing-limited at ~40 MHz by the DSP-output-to-32-bit carry-chain accumulator route plus pad fanout, pipeline the multipliers and input, register DSP outputs, shrink the accumulator to 29 bits, and go symmetric, cutting DSPs 16->8 and LUTs 1220->1015 while raising Fmax to 55.8 MHz (+16.1 MHz) by splitting the 25.15 ns path and removing the 6.1 ns pad-to-multiplier fanout.

When a transposed symmetric GateMate FIR is routing-critical at 55.8 MHz and has no DSP-output-to-accumulator pipeline, avoid maximum DSP input/output register insertion (pipe_mul 1→3, dsp_regs=in_out), because on this device it increases the critical route from 4.2 to 6.32 ns and lowers Fmax to 54.6 MHz instead of splitting the path.

When a symmetric, DSP-registered transposed FIR on GateMate is routing-limited at 54.56 MHz with a 6.32 ns route in the critical path, keep the symmetric/DSP-registered structure rather than switching to a non-symmetric 16-multiplier form with only two multiplier pipe stages and no DSP I/O registers, since that change doubled DSP use (8→16), added 86 LUTs, and lowered Fmax by 3.5 MHz to 51.11 MHz without shortening the multiplier-to-accumulator route.

When a 16-tap transposed FIR on GateMate is timing-limited by the 5.46 ns high-fanout route into 16 multiplier operands, make it symmetric and insert DSP input/pipe/output registers to halve multipliers to 8 and operand loads to 8, cutting route delay to 5.17 ns and raising Fmax 51.1→55.2 MHz (+4.1) with 86 fewer LUTs.

When a transposed symmetric GateMate FIR is timing-limited at 55.2 MHz by a 5.17 ns high-fanout route into the 8 pre-adder/multiplier operands, do not fold 1→2 and drop pipe_mul 2→1 while setting dsp_regs=in_pipe_out/out; it halves DSPs 8→4 but doubles the operand-broadcast route to 10.34 ns and drops Fmax to 43.74 MHz, so keep fold=1 and instead insert the in* DSP register after the pre-adder.

When a GateMate transposed FIR is timing-limited at ~40 MHz by the DSP-output-to-32-bit carry-chain accumulator route plus pad fanout, pipeline the multipliers and input, register DSP outputs, shrink the accumulator to 29 bits, and go symmetric, cutting DSPs 16->8 and LUTs 1220->1015 while raising Fmax to 55.8 MHz (+16.1 MHz) by splitting the 25.15 ns path and removing the 6.1 ns pad-to-multiplier fanout.

When a GateMate FIR is timing-limited at 55.84 MHz by a 4.2 ns coefficient-register-to-multiplier route that is 48% of the 17.91 ns path under pipe_mul=1, do not add fabric registers at the DSP input/output boundary: it was neutral-to-worse (fmax 54.82 MHz, LUT +2 to 1017, DSP 8, route 4.2→5.34 ns) because the extra reg-to-reg hop did not break the placement-congestion-sensitive multiplier-boundary routing.

When a symmetric transposed FIR on GateMate is timing-limited by the fabric-register-to-DSP input route at 54.8 MHz with fold=1 and 8 DSPs, avoid folding to 2 to halve DSPs to 4, because the input route worsens from 5.34 to 9.17 ns and the critical path grows from 18.24 to 23.25 ns, dropping fmax to 43.0 MHz (-11.8 MHz) for only 4 fewer DSPs and 7 more LUTs.

When a folded symmetric FIR on the GateMate is timing-limited by the 4.2 ns coefficient-RF route into the DSP multiplier (43.0 MHz), dropping fold=2 to fold=1 and enabling in_out registers on both multiplier ports splits that input route into two short hops, lifting fmax to 56.3 MHz (+13.3 MHz) for +4 DSPs and -8 LUTs.

When a GateMate symmetric transposed FIR is timing-limited by ~5.8 ns of coefficient/tap fan-out routing into DSP columns at 56.28 MHz, do not add a second post-multiplier fabric pipeline stage (pipe_mul 1->2), because it raised the critical path from 17.77 to 18.27 ns and dropped Fmax to 54.73 MHz for +1 LUT and no DSP benefit—the bottleneck is interconnect, not multiplier pipeline depth.

When a GateMate transposed FIR is timing-limited at ~40 MHz by the DSP-output-to-32-bit carry-chain accumulator route plus pad fanout, pipeline the multipliers and input, register DSP outputs, shrink the accumulator to 29 bits, and go symmetric, cutting DSPs 16->8 and LUTs 1220->1015 while raising Fmax to 55.8 MHz (+16.1 MHz) by splitting the 25.15 ns path and removing the 6.1 ns pad-to-multiplier fanout.

When a GateMate symmetric transposed FIR is timing-limited by the pre-multiplier routing (5.34 ns net through the symmetric pre-adder LUT, with ~7.5 ns DSP-internal delay fixed), remove the redundant fabric pipeline stage at the already-registered DSP output (pipe_mul 1→0 with dsp_regs=out): it cuts 3 LUTs and the worst route to 4.56 ns for 54.8→55.2 MHz, but expect only a neutral gain because the symmetric delay-line operand routing and DSP-internal path still dominate.

When a symmetric transposed GateMate FIR is timing-limited by the 4.56 ns coefficient route into the DSP operand LUT at 55.2 MHz with 8 DSPs and an 18.13 ns critical path, register both DSP operand inputs and outputs to place a local capture register at the multiplier boundary, yielding only +1.4 MHz to 56.6 MHz because the operand/coefficient-net routing and 8.6 ns CC_MULT remain the limiter.

When a transposed symmetric FIR on GateMate is pinned at ~56 MHz by a routing-dominated path (5.3 ns launching net into the DSP plus ~7 ns of the adjacent-cell CC_MULT cascade), adding a multiplier output pipeline register (pipe_mul 0→1) buys nothing (−0.3 MHz, +1 LUT) because DSP register knobs only re-roll those nets within ±0.5 ns instead of shortening the cascade.

When a GateMate transposed symmetric FIR at 56.28 MHz is timing-limited by ~5.8 ns routing into the 8 DSP multiplier operands rather than the accumulator or IO, do not add a second fabric stage after the multiplier (pipe_mul 1->2): it lowered Fmax to 54.73 MHz for +1 LUT because the operand/distribution route remains the bottleneck, so reduce the multiplier array/fold instead.

For a symmetric transposed FIR on GateMate that is routing-bound at fold=1/8 DSPs (54.7 MHz, 18.27 ns critical path), fold to 4 MACs and set pipe_mul=1 to halve operand fanout and split mux/ROM→multiply from multiply→carry-chain add, lifting Fmax to 60.3 MHz (+5.6) and making 16.58 ns feasible at +11 LUTs/−4 DSPs.
